purpose: Unstick players; teach record-vs-truth without spoiling adjudication.
rules: Hints escalate from attention → comparison → method → soft direction. Never name Martha as the answer before the player commits.
Never say ‘desertion is the hinge’ or ‘supportable widow is Martha’ in early rungs.
Sealed D018 never appears in hints.
Separate hint packet from player packet (Binder).

rungs.when_stuck: Overwhelmed by dual claims / death paper naming Lydia
rungs.hint: List what each claimant asserts in her own words — marriage date, death claim, and what would make her file look strong. Don’t decide yet.

rungs.when_stuck: Hasn’t verified marriages or treats claims as proof
rungs.hint: Find the marriage registers for the dates and counties each woman cites. Treat each register as a witness to a ceremony — not yet as the final law.

rungs.when_stuck: Accepts hospital death as settled / ignores muster
rungs.hint: Pull both the hospital line and the company muster for the same man. Write down how each describes his fate. If they disagree, that disagreement is evidence.
A death register naming a wife tells you who the household presented as widow. Separately ask: was there an earlier marriage, and was it ever dissolved?
rungs.teaches: Named widow ≠ only possible / supportable widow.

rungs.when_stuck: Hasn’t found postwar life / still thinks 1863 death
rungs.hint: After the wartime papers, look for the soldier in later censuses in the county of the second marriage. Ask whether a man marked dead can still appear as head of household.
rungs.teaches: Recorded death vs continued life on paper.

rungs.when_stuck: Tempted by Corbin/Ashley divorce or unsure about dissolution
rungs.hint: When a divorce decree looks close, compare every letter of both surnames to the couple you care about. Then check the search result that names your exact parties.
rungs.teaches: Near-name ≠ same persons; use the negative search for the right couple.

rungs.when_stuck: Confused by Silas Corbit hospital death
rungs.hint: Same-ish surnames aren’t identity. Match unit, age, and home county before merging two hospital lines.
rungs.teaches: Require more than a shared name.

rungs.when_stuck: Ready to commit but conflating ceremony with lawful status
rungs.hint: Separate three questions: (1) Did each ceremony happen? (2) Did an earlier undissolved marriage still bind? (3) Who does the death paper name? Answer each from paper before you pick a supportable widow.
rungs.teaches: Ceremony ≠ lawful; death naming ≠ marriage law.
rungs.soft_direction: Still does not name Martha; forces the three-question frame that yields Martha.
